questions.stem: The Election Commission of India is established under which Article of the Constitution?
questions.explanation: ARTICLE 324 — 'Superintendence, direction and control of elections to be vested in an Election Commission'. The ECI supervises elections to Parliament, State Legislatures, offices of President + Vice-President. DOES NOT conduct local body elections (handled by STATE Election Commissions under Arts 243K + 243ZA — different body, added by 73rd + 74th CAA 1992). FOUNDED: 25 JANUARY 1950 — one day before Republic Day; this date is now celebrated as NATIONAL VOTERS' DAY since 2011. FIRST CEC: SUKUMAR SEN (IAS, 1950-58) — ran the massive 1st general election 1951-52 (17.3 crore eligible voters). CONSTITUTION-BODY CATEGORY: CONSTITUTIONAL body (unlike NITI Aayog, CBI, CVC which are statutory/executive). STRUCTURE: started with just CEC; became MULTI-MEMBER in Oct 1989; permanent 3-member since 1993 (CEC + 2 ECs — all equal status + equal vote). Decisions by majority if they disagree. ADMIN: secretariat at Nirvachan Sadan, New Delhi. APPOINTMENT: by PRESIDENT, per recent 2023 Act, on advice of 3-member panel (PM + LoP + Union Minister nominated by PM). TERM: 6 YEARS or until 65 — whichever earlier. REMOVAL: CEC can be removed ONLY by parliamentary IMPEACHMENT (like SC judge); ECs can be removed on CEC's recommendation.

questions.stem: The ELECTION COMMISSION of India became a MULTI-MEMBER body permanently from:

options.option_text: 1 OCTOBER 1993 — under PM Narasimha Rao (after brief multi-member 1989-90 phase + reversal)

questions.explanation: ECI — MULTI-MEMBER status chronology: (1) 1950-1989: SINGLE-member body (only CEC). (2) 16 Oct 1989: Rajiv Gandhi government appointed two ECs making it a 3-member body for the first time (controversial — seen as PM's attempt to undermine independent CEC RVS Peri Sastri). (3) 2 January 1990: V.P. Singh's Janata Dal government ABOLISHED the two EC posts — returned to single-member. (4) 1 OCTOBER 1993: Narasimha Rao Cabinet permanently made ECI a 3-member body — CEC T.N. SESHAN was making aggressive moves solo, so adding 2 ECs was seen as a CHECK on him; SESHAN (CEC 1990-96) challenged the constitutionality; SC upheld it in T.N. SESHAN v. UNION OF INDIA (1995). Today's structure: 1 CEC + 2 ECs; all have EQUAL voting power; decisions by majority. RANK: CEC = rank of SC judge (salary, status); EC = rank of SC judge now too (after 2022 equalisation). ALL Commission members appointed by the President. T.N. SESHAN's tenure (1990-96) TRANSFORMED the ECI: enforced MODEL CODE OF CONDUCT strictly, issued voter ID cards (EPIC), cracked down on electoral malpractices (booth capturing, paid news, bribery). Called the 'Indian Eliot Ness'; RAMON MAGSAYSAY award 1996. Died Nov 2019.

questions.stem: NATIONAL VOTERS' DAY is celebrated on:

options.option_text: 25 JANUARY — foundation day of ECI (established 25 Jan 1950, one day before Republic Day)

questions.explanation: NATIONAL VOTERS' DAY (NVD) — celebrated on 25 JANUARY every year to mark the FOUNDATION DAY of the ECI (25 January 1950, one day before Republic Day). Started in 2011 by President Pratibha Patil. OBJECTIVE: (1) encourage young voters (aged 18+) to ENROL in electoral rolls + collect their voter ID (EPIC); (2) spread electoral awareness + participation. CONDUCTED at booth level across 10+ lakh polling stations on 25 Jan every year. EACH YEAR has a theme — 'Nothing Like Voting, I Vote for Sure' etc. BEST ELECTORAL PRACTICES AWARDS: presented to states, DEOs, NGOs + media on NVD. SVEEP (Systematic Voters' Education and Electoral Participation) is the ECI's flagship programme for voter awareness. WORLD ELECTION: India is the LARGEST democracy — 2024 Lok Sabha elections had 96.88 crore registered voters (~97 crore), 64.64 crore voted (turnout ~66.14%). The 2024 election was the largest democratic exercise in human history. First general elections 1951-52 had 17.3 crore voters + took 4 months. Voter ID (EPIC) first issued 1993 under CEC T.N. Seshan. Voting age lowered from 21 to 18 by 61st CAA (1989) — effective from 1989 general election.

questions.stem: Who was the FIRST WOMAN to serve as CHIEF ELECTION COMMISSIONER of India?

options.option_text: V.S. RAMA DEVI — served as CEC for just 17 days (26 Nov – 11 Dec 1990)

questions.explanation: V.S. RAMA DEVI (1934-2013) — FIRST WOMAN CEC of India; held the post 26 Nov 1990 – 11 Dec 1990 (just 17 DAYS — the SHORTEST tenure of any CEC). Background: brilliant legal mind; PRIOR = Union Legislative Secretary + first woman Secretary-General of Lok Sabha (1993-97). POST-CEC: later served as GOVERNOR of Himachal Pradesh (1997-99) + GOVERNOR of Karnataka (1999-2002). Her brief tenure as CEC was due to political manoeuvring — PM Chandra Shekhar's short-lived government. She was replaced by T.N. Seshan. NO woman has served as CEC since. First EC (NOT CEC): Smt. LEELA SETH — not; first female Election Commissioner (EC) was V.S. Rama Devi (she was EC before promotion). More recently: PADMA SUBRAHMANIAM — no, never CEC. As of 2026, the current CEC is Rajiv Kumar → Gyanesh Kumar (feb 2025). FIRST CEC overall: SUKUMAR SEN (1950-58). LONGEST-SERVING CEC: R.V.S. Peri Sastri (1986-90). 25 CECs served as of Feb 2025. OTHER NOTABLE FIRSTS: First WOMAN State EC — some states have had; First WOMAN Speaker of Lok Sabha: MEIRA KUMAR (2009-14) succeeded by SUMITRA MAHAJAN (2014-19).

questions.stem: The MODEL CODE OF CONDUCT (MCC) issued by the Election Commission:

options.option_text: Is a statutory law enforceable in court
Is a set of GUIDELINES evolved by political parties through CONSENSUS — morally binding, not legally enforceable; enforced by ECI
Was passed as a constitutional amendment
Applies only to the ruling party

questions.explanation: MODEL CODE OF CONDUCT (MCC) — a set of NORMS issued by the ECI for political parties + candidates during elections. EVOLUTION: first adopted in Kerala during 1960 assembly elections; gradually accepted by all major parties; formalised by ECI in its present form in 1991 (T.N. Seshan-era strict enforcement). STATUS: NOT a law; not enforceable in courts; moral + political commitment among parties. But ECI ENFORCES it via its Art 324 powers — can de-register parties, disqualify candidates for grave violations. OPERATES from the date of ELECTION ANNOUNCEMENT (not notification) until the election process is completed. KEY PROVISIONS: (1) Parties/candidates must not (a) aggravate communal tensions; (b) use/abuse govt machinery for party work; (c) make promises using taxpayers' money just before election; (d) criticise private lives of opponents. (2) RULING PARTY under special restrictions: no new project announcements, no transfers of key officials without ECI clearance, no use of govt guest houses for party events, no use of govt funds for vehicles/ads. VIOLATIONS: 'censure', FIR under RPA/IPC, notice-issuing for explanation. HISTORIC CASES: 2019 MCC violations against Modi + Rahul over speeches; 2022 Yogi 'Abba Jaan' speech violation. Some parties have demanded MCC be given LEGAL TEETH; ECI opposes — flexibility + speed more valuable.

questions.stem: ELECTRONIC VOTING MACHINES (EVMs) were FIRST USED in a general election in India in:

options.option_text: 2004 — first GENERAL ELECTION where EVMs were used NATIONWIDE; EVMs had been used in phases from 1999

questions.explanation: EVM CHRONOLOGY in India: (1) 1977 — EVM concept developed by ECI with Electronics Corp. of India (ECIL) + Bharat Electronics (BEL). (2) 1982 — FIRST USE: PARUR assembly constituency BY-election in Kerala (50 polling stations). Result was challenged in court (AC George v. State — SC ruled EVM use was ultra vires; Parliament needed to amend RPA). (3) 1989 — RPA amended to legally permit EVMs. (4) 1998 — EVMs used in select constituencies of Rajasthan, MP, Delhi. (5) 1999 — used in 46 Lok Sabha constituencies. (6) 2001 — first FULL STATE election: Tamil Nadu (also Kerala, Puducherry, WB). (7) 2004 GENERAL ELECTION — FIRST FULL LOK SABHA election conducted entirely on EVMs (all 543 seats). ALL ELECTIONS since 2004 have used EVMs. (8) 2013 — VVPAT (Voter Verifiable Paper Audit Trail) introduced in Nagaland by-election; 2019 LS was the first GE with VVPAT at ALL booths. COMPONENTS: Control Unit (with Presiding Officer) + Ballot Unit (in the voting compartment); max 16 candidates per BU; up to 4 BUs cascadable for 64 candidates; machines run on batteries (no mains power needed). TAMPERING: ECI maintains EVMs are STANDALONE (not networked) + one-time programmable (OTP chips) + tamper-evident. SC has repeatedly upheld integrity. CRITICS demand return to ballot papers. TOTAL EVMs deployed 2024 GE: ~55 lakh units.

questions.stem: NOTA (None Of The Above) option on EVMs was introduced following a 2013 Supreme Court judgment. Which case?

options.option_text: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
PEOPLE'S UNION FOR CIVIL LIBERTIES (PUCL) v. UNION OF INDIA (2013) — SC directed ECI to provide NOTA on ballot paper / EVM
Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India

questions.explanation: PUCL v. UNION OF INDIA (27 Sep 2013) — landmark SC judgment directing ECI to include a NOTA (None Of The Above) button on EVMs + ballot papers to enable voters to reject ALL candidates. Based on the FUNDAMENTAL RIGHT under Art 19(1)(a) (speech + expression — vote = expression) + Right to negative vote. FIRST USE: 2013 state assembly elections (Delhi, Chhattisgarh, MP, Rajasthan, Mizoram). NOTA SYMBOL: a ballot paper with a CROSS marked through it, designed by NID Ahmedabad. EFFECT: currently purely SYMBOLIC — even if NOTA gets more votes than any candidate, the candidate with the highest NON-NOTA votes still wins. Parties with NOTA-HIGH constituencies see political pressure. Some countries (Russia, Ukraine had 'against all' option earlier). 2024 Lok Sabha: Indore saw Congress candidate withdraw late → NOTA got 2.18 LAKH votes (second place; highest NOTA vote share ever in a single LS seat — 14%). ECI has proposed binding NOTA — if NOTA wins, election be re-held with new candidates — but PARLIAMENT has not legislated this. MAHARASHTRA State Election Commission (for local body polls) has made NOTA the de-facto 'fictional elected candidate' — if NOTA leads, re-polling. Goa ordered similar in 2023. NOTA turnout typically 1-2% nationally; rises to 4-5% in constituencies with weak candidates.

questions.stem: The minimum age to CONTEST a Lok Sabha election is:

options.option_text: 25 YEARS — as per Article 84(b) of the Constitution + Section 4 of the RPA 1951

questions.explanation: AGE REQUIREMENTS to CONTEST Indian elections — per the Constitution: (1) LOK SABHA + State Legislative Assembly: 25 years (Art 84(b), 173(b)). (2) RAJYA SABHA + State Legislative Council: 30 years (Art 84(b) for RS; Art 173(b) for LC). (3) PRESIDENT of India: 35 years (Art 58(1)(b)). (4) VICE-PRESIDENT of India: 35 years (Art 66(3)(b)). (5) GOVERNOR of State: 35 years (Art 157). VOTING age: 18 YEARS (reduced from 21 by 61st CAA 1989 by Rajiv Gandhi government). OTHER DISQUALIFICATIONS for contesting (Art 102 + RPA 1951): (a) unsound mind declared by competent court; (b) undischarged insolvent; (c) holding office of profit under Government; (d) non-citizen of India; (e) conviction for certain offences (RPA Sec 8 — if convicted >2 years jail, disqualified for 6 years after release; Lily Thomas v. UoI, 2013 — SC ruled conviction causes IMMEDIATE disqualification from membership, not just contesting). (f) Failure to lodge election expenses. (g) disqualification under ANTI-DEFECTION LAW (10th Schedule). NO EDUCATIONAL qualification mandated at central level for LS/Assembly; some states have imposed them for PANCHAYAT elections (SC upheld Haryana's min qualification in 2015 Rajbala case — controversially).

questions.stem: The CURRENT ceiling on ELECTION EXPENDITURE for a Lok Sabha candidate (as of 2022 revision) is:

options.option_text: ₹95 LAKH (bigger states) / ₹75 LAKH (smaller states) — revised by ECI Jan 2022 from earlier ₹70/54 L

questions.explanation: ELECTION EXPENDITURE LIMITS — set by ECI via Conduct of Election Rules 1961, periodically revised. CURRENT limits (revised Jan 2022 based on ECI committee): (1) LOK SABHA — ₹95 LAKH (big states: AP, UP, TN, Maha, etc.) / ₹75 LAKH (small states + UTs: Goa, Sikkim, Arunachal, etc.). (2) VIDHAN SABHA — ₹40 LAKH (big states) / ₹28 LAKH (small states). Earlier 2014-2022: ₹70L LS big, ₹54L LS small. RATIONALE: account for inflation, rising campaign costs (media, GPS-tagged vehicles, mobile app costs). REPORTING: candidates must LODGE EXPENDITURE within 30 days of result; penalty for not doing so = disqualification for 3 years. TRACKING: ECI deploys Flying Squads, Video Surveillance Teams, Static Surveillance Teams, Accounting Teams. SEIZED cash/liquor/freebies during 2024 LS: ~₹10,000+ crore (highest ever). POLITICAL PARTIES: NO CEILING on party expenditure (only candidate; a loophole parties exploit heavily for 'party publicity'). Voluntary disclosure norms by ECI + IT returns filing. ELECTORAL BONDS (2018-2024) were struck down by SC in Feb 2024 (ADR v. UOI) — anonymity + unlimited corp donations unconstitutional; ordered SBI to disclose donor list. REGISTERED PARTIES: over 2,500 (as of 2024); only ~6 national + 50+ state parties.

questions.stem: The VVPAT (Voter Verifiable Paper Audit Trail) was introduced to:

options.option_text: PROVIDE A PAPER RECORD of each EVM vote, visible to the voter briefly, to allow VERIFICATION + audit in case of disputes

questions.explanation: VVPAT (Voter Verifiable Paper Audit Trail) — an ATTACHMENT to the EVM that prints a PAPER SLIP showing the voter's choice (candidate name + party symbol) for ~7 SECONDS after the voter presses the EVM button. Slip is visible through a TRANSPARENT window, then drops into a SEALED BOX (voter does not take it). PURPOSE: (a) allow voter to VERIFY her vote was recorded correctly; (b) provide a PAPER AUDIT TRAIL for manual recount in case of dispute; (c) address EVM-tampering allegations. HISTORY: (1) 2010 ECI ordered trials. (2) 2013 FIRST USED in Nagaland (Noksen AC by-election). (3) SEP 2013: SC in Subramanian Swamy v. ECI ruled VVPAT is 'indispensable for free + fair elections'. (4) 2019 Lok Sabha — first GENERAL ELECTION with VVPAT at ALL booths. (5) 2019 SC direction: 5 VVPAT SLIPS per assembly segment to be manually counted + matched with EVM — now standard. 2024 FURTHER PILs for 100% VVPAT-EVM matching were DISMISSED by SC (Apr 2024) — ruled existing 5-booth sample sufficient; 100% match not needed. VVPAT UNITS: ~17 lakh deployed in 2024 GE. MANUFACTURED by BEL + ECIL. NOT connected to any network; thermal printer with special ink; requires dry + dust-free storage.
